claim: Early dynamic-memory CBR (CYRUS E-MOPs, IPP) organised episodes under generalised norms with discriminating indices, and was evaluated only by worked examples on hand-built narrow domains. No quantitative human or accuracy test exists.
agent_test: Do not cite early-CBR numbers as evidence; treat as design inspiration only.

claim: Generalising from the first two shared-index episodes and revising norms by later evidence is the core update rule (certainty not judged before 6 events; sub-MOPs absorbed into parent). Its error rate was never measured.
agent_test: Ablate: promote a lesson to a norm after 2 vs 4 vs 6 confirming episodes; measure wrong-lesson rate and accuracy at equal tokens.

claim: Limiting the index vocabulary to salient features prevents memory blow-up; features true of nearly all events stay as norms, not indices.
agent_test: Compare tag-restricted case keys vs all-feature keys on retrieval precision and prompt tokens.

claim: Retrieval fails when the cue does not name the discriminating index; remedies are schema triggering, inferring index values, and following related events (cue elaboration).
agent_test: Add a cue-elaboration step before retrieval (LLM infers missing situation features) vs raw query embedding; compare hit rate.

claim: Whether human memory is organised by events or episodic MOPs, and whether retrieval slows with memory size (fan effect), was left open as human-data questions; the Bower-Black-Turner and Reiser results were not opened this session.
agent_test: Not testable on the agent; needs primary human sources.

claim: Providing an LLM agent with a case bank of past episodes raises accuracy over the same agent without it (Memento DeepResearcher 59.9/72.2 F1/PM to 66.6/80.4; HLE 17.4 to 24.4 PM).
agent_test: Equal-token ablation: scaffold with vs without a case bank on a held-out task stream.

claim: Much of the case-memory gain is confounded with repeated attempts and tools: the no-CBR Memento variant climbs 78.65 to 84.47 over 5 iterations; CBR adds only 1.2-1.8 points at iteration 1 and 0.4-1.0 at iteration 5. Gap-search addition: in ReasoningBank (web tasks) memory-less best-of-5 gains only +3.2 (39.0 to 42.2) while memory plus best-of-5 reaches 55.1 from 49.7, so on that benchmark the memory gain is not just extra attempts.
agent_test: Always compare against a no-memory arm given the same number of attempts and tokens (best-of-N control).

claim: A small number of retrieved cases (about 1 to 4) is enough; more adds nothing or hurts (Memento K=4 best 64.5 F1, K=32 63.9; DS-Agent more than one case degrades; CBR-RAG k=3).
agent_test: Sweep k = 1,2,4,8 at fixed total context; expect plateau near 3-4.

claim: Retrieval keyed on task similarity beats random or reasoning-similarity selection (ExpeL ALFWorld: ReAct 40.0, random 42.5, reasoning-similarity 48.5, task-similarity 59.0).
agent_test: Index cases by situation/task features; compare to random and to reasoning-trace-keyed retrieval.

claim: Extracted abstractions (insights/strategies/workflows) combined with episode retrieval beat either alone in some domains; the better mode differs by task (insights-only vs retrieval-only HotpotQA 36 vs 31, ALFWorld 50 vs 55).
agent_test: Three arms: raw episodes, distilled lessons, both; report per task type.

claim: Distilled strategy memory from successes and failures beats raw-trajectory and workflow memory (ReasoningBank WebArena flash 48.8 vs AWM 44.1, Synapse 42.1, none 40.5).
agent_test: Store failure-derived lessons with a what-went-wrong field; compare success-only vs both at equal memory size.

claim: Adding failed trajectories helps strong distillation but can hurt weaker memory designs (Shopping: ReasoningBank 46.5 to 49.7; AWM 44.4 to 42.2; Evo-Memory baselines degrade under unfiltered failures).
agent_test: Test failure storage with and without a quality filter.

claim: Agents imitate the most similar stored record (experience-following), so unfiltered add-all memory is harmful: RegAgent 55.48 add-all vs 67.53 fixed memory vs 70.95 strict add; EHRAgent 13.05 vs 16.75 vs 38.50.
agent_test: Gate memory writes by a verified-success signal; compare add-all vs gated writes.

claim: Utility-based deletion shrinks memory about 4x at small accuracy cost and kept records are more often correct than deleted ones.
agent_test: Periodic pruning of low-utility cases; measure accuracy vs memory size.

claim: Wrong or mismatched stored cases can hurt: gains vanish with weak backbones or weak checks (Reflexion starchat-beta 0.26 vs 0.26; Dynamic Cheatsheet GPT-4o-mini AIME24 16.7 to 13.3; AWM on Claude 40.8 vs 41.7 none). Counter-case: ReasoningBank lifts Gemma-3-12B 17.1 to 24.1 on WebArena-Shopping while raw-trajectory Synapse falls to 16.0, so the threshold depends on memory form.
agent_test: Run memory ablation per backbone strength; do not assume memory transfers to weak models.

claim: Memory gains track within-dataset task similarity (Evo-Memory ReMem gain correlation r=0.717 Gemini 2.5 Flash, 0.563 Claude 3.7 Sonnet) and recurring task structure; low-similarity sets such as AIME-25 and GPQA gain little.
agent_test: Measure gain as a function of case-to-task similarity; skip memory when similarity is low.

claim: Dynamic Cheatsheet gives very large gains on tasks with reusable structure (GPT-4o Game of 24 10 to 99 by storing a Python solution; Claude 3.5 Sonnet AIME24 23.3 to 50.0) and storing full history can hurt (GPT-4o AIME24 13.3 vs 20.0 baseline).
agent_test: Test curated rewrite vs append-all history at equal tokens.

claim: Reflection-style episodic buffers (1 to 3 reflections) improve repeated attempts when a reliable binary success signal exists (Reflexion ALFWorld 130 of 134 in 12 trials; HumanEval 91.0 vs 80.1) and fail where tests are weak (MBPP 77.1 vs 80.1).
agent_test: Use reflections only when a trusted verifier exists.

claim: The generative-agents memory stream (recency, importance, relevance retrieval + reflection) ablation: full 29.89, no reflection 26.88, no reflection/planning 25.64, no memory 21.21 TrueSkill; KW chi2(4)=150.29.
agent_test: Believability is human-rated and not task accuracy; use only as design precedent.

claim: Skill libraries of verified programs retrieved by description speed learning (Voyager 3.3x more unique items; diamond pickaxe 19 +/- 3 iterations vs 36).
agent_test: Store only verified procedures; CoALA warns procedural writes carry bug risk.

claim: Elaborate memory systems often lose to simply reading the full context when it fits: Mem0 full-context 72.90 vs 68.44 (Mem0g) vs 66.88 (Mem0); MemoryAgentBench long-context 48.8-60.6 vs agentic memory 18.7-37.7; LongMemEval ~30% drop.
agent_test: Control arm: put the whole history in context; use memory only when it does not fit or must be cheaper (Mem0 p95 latency 1.44 s vs 17.1 s).

claim: Linked self-organising note memory (A-Mem) claimed gains on LoCoMo that an independent re-run did not reproduce (A-Mem 48.38 J overall vs full-context 72.90, a 20-point gap to Mem0g; category-level lags exceed 25 points). A second third-party benchmark (EvolMem) has A-MEM at 44.54 vs base 52.18.
agent_test: Do not adopt note-linking without own replication.

claim: Structured case-based pipelines help only slightly in legal QA (CBR-RAG +1.94% cosine, 32 test cases) and CBR retrieval in fallacy classification improves F1 2.5-6 points but not by copying labels (label overlap 27.7%); added counterarguments or explanations matter.
agent_test: Present retrieved cases with an explanation or contrast rather than label only.

claim: Transformers trained on arithmetic behave like case matchers rather than rule users (Llama-2-7B base-9 addition 30.2% in leave-square-out vs 92% random split); explicit rule-following fine-tuning fixes it.
agent_test: Check the agent on held-out regions of a task family; do not infer rule use from in-distribution success.

claim: Semi-parametric experience memory with Q-values needs few tasks (Rememberer used 10 training tasks vs 10,587 for RL; WebShop 0.39 vs ReAct 0.36), gain small.
agent_test: Add a utility score per case updated from outcomes.

claim: No benchmark yet isolates CBR-specific memory design for LLM agents; the available review reports almost no figures.
agent_test: Build own benchmark: same stream, same tokens, memory designs varied.

claim: On web tasks, a distilled-strategy memory plus best-of-N beats best-of-N without memory by a wide margin at equal rollouts (Shopping k=5: 55.1 vs 42.2). Not yet tested on pure reasoning tasks with a frontier model.
agent_test: Run best-of-5 with and without lesson memory on our reasoning set at matched total tokens.

claim: A coarse LLM judge as write gate is nearly as good as an oracle for strategy-style memory: judge accuracy 72.7 percent; success rate stays within about 2 to 5 points of oracle from 90 percent down to 50 percent simulated accuracy.
agent_test: Compare write gates (oracle, self-judge, none) on our tasks; keep the oracle for raw-trajectory stores.

claim: Task keywords extracted by an LLM give a better retrieval key than a raw task embedding, and both beat random cases (TravelPlanner commonsense: GPT-4o 76.02 / 73.38 / 74.59; no memory 71.93). Random cases still help, which suggests part of the gain is generic guidance.
agent_test: Include a random-case control in every memory ablation.

claim: Spurious generalisation from two instances was observed by Lebowitz (UNIMEM refines by dropping unreliable features; IPP could not), but no wrong-lesson rate exists for early CBR or for LLM-written lessons.
agent_test: Measure wrong-lesson rate: after promotion, test each lesson on held-out cases; demote if it fails.

claim: No independent reproduction of AWM was found; A-Mem has only third-party evaluations on other benchmarks. Primary human foundation studies (Bower-Black-Turner, Reiser, Williams-Hollan, Schank 1982) remain unopened. Cue elaboration for episode memory is untested; HyDE query elaboration gives +12 to +16 nDCG@10 for document retrieval only.
agent_test: Treat these as open; do not cite as established.
